[d/g532e4d229a6c-1] decision (cited, source git:532e4d229a6c98c1cb4b98ba9709a1179deb897f)
  Add six binary tests for cmd_fmt covering listed fmt decisions.
  Twelve mutants survived in cmd_fmt because nothing reached the command through the binary. The tests drive the binary as a user would, killing mutants in those decisions and reducing survivors from 12 to 2.

[d/g532e4d229a6c-2] decision (cited, source git:532e4d229a6c98c1cb4b98ba9709a1179deb897f)
  Do not write a test for the round-trip guard; record it as a known survivor.
  The guard fires only when write_surface produces something the parser reads back differently, and no user input can reach it. A test cannot distinguish a guard that checks from one that does not, so the author records it like previous untestable cases with a pointer to the tests covering the property it protects.

[d/g532e4d229a6c-3] decision (cited, source tests/cmd_fmt.rs@532e4d229a6c)
  Make each test write its own document with the needed property instead of using repository fixtures.
  The first version depended on repository fixtures like F1 not canonical and F9 having comments. cargo-mutants reuses build directories, so a mutant that misroutes a write can leave a fixture rewritten, causing spurious failures counted as catches. The rule is that a test must not depend on the state of the tree, just as it must not depend on the state of the machine.

[d/g87345653cdf3-10] decision (cited, source tests/doc_output.rs@87345653cdf3)

  The first version asserted only that MISMATCHED appeared, which ran 0 transcripts satisfied; the count assertion ensures a gate that cannot confuse nothing wrong with nothing checked.
